label: prf:knot-operator-selection
title: Proof of knot operator selection
html:
Proof sketch

(i) The Hecke algebra H_r(q) is semisimple for generic q, so \mathrm{End}_{H_r(q)}(V^{\otimes r}) decomposes as \bigoplus_\lambda \mathrm{End}(V_\lambda) by the Wedderburn theorem. The Markov trace projects onto each component with weight d_\lambda(q) by Schur orthogonality (RJ inner product).

(ii) The categorical action \mathfrak{S} = \mathrm{ev}_A \circ (\mathrm{id}_{A^\vee} \otimes \Phi) \circ \mathrm{coev}_A = \mathrm{tr}(\Phi) is linear in \Phi. Substituting the spectral decomposition (i) and using the identification \mathrm{tr} = \mathrm{tr}_M (archimedean descent, RJ interpretation) gives the stated sum over channels.

(iii) The Frobenius pairing \langle a, b \rangle_F = \int_A \mu(a \otimes b) = \mathrm{tr}_M(\rho(\hat\beta_a) \cdot \rho(\hat\beta_b)) is the categorical inner product. Non-degeneracy (QUO-1) means every element has a unique Frobenius dual. In the NF basis, this identifies positive coefficients with morphisms \mathbf{1} \to A (supply, via coevaluation) and negative coefficients with morphisms A \to \mathbf{1} (demand, via evaluation).

(iv) The on-shell condition constrains \Phi to lie in the self-dual curvature subspace (S([\sigma_i, \sigma_j])^* = [\sigma_i, \sigma_j]). Within this subspace, the extremum of |\mathrm{tr}(\Phi)| is attained at the irrep with largest quantum dimension times character evaluation. For pair production at our q_0 = 1.109978595642739\ldots (muon pin, 16 dps), this is T_{2,3} (trefoil, e^-) — the lowest-crossing operator that unconditionally opens the degree-3 channel.

Explicit dual construction

Consider a state K \in H_3(q) with decomposition K = \sum_i c_i b_i. The Frobenius dual K^\vee is the unique element satisfying

  \langle K^\vee, b_i \rangle_F = c_i
  \quad \forall i.

By non-degeneracy (convention D: read on the quotient H_n/\mathrm{rad}\,\mathrm{tr}_M \cong \mathrm{TL}_n, where the induced pairing is non-degenerate; on H_n itself \det G = 0 exactly, the (1^3) block being the radical — MarkovGramDegenerate.lean), K^\vee exists and is unique. In the basis, K^\vee = \sum_i c_i (G^{-1})_{ij} b_j, where G_{ij} = \langle b_i, b_j \rangle_F = \mathrm{tr}_M(b_i \cdot b_j) is the 6 \times 6 Gram matrix of H_3(q).

The demand vector of K is the negative part:

  \mathrm{dem}(K) = \sum_{i : c_i < 0} |c_i| \, b_i^\vee.

The operator that fills the demand at minimum crossing energy is

  \Phi_{\mathrm{min}}
  =
  \arg\min_{\Phi \in \mathrm{End}(A)_{\mathrm{on-shell}}}
  \left\{
    \mathfrak{E}_{\mathrm{cross}}(\Phi)
    \ \Big|\ 
    \langle \Phi, \mathrm{dem}(K) \rangle_F \geq
    \|\mathrm{dem}(K)\|_F
  \right\}.

For the positron (e^+ = \sigma_0^{-1}\sigma_1^{-1}\sigma_0^{-1}), the demand profile is \{-0.218\gamma, -0.209 L_+, -0.209 L_-\}. The mirror trefoil demands vacuum energy and Hopf content. The minimum-energy supply is the coevaluation \mathrm{coev}_A \colon \mathbf{1} \to A \otimes A^\vee, which provides exactly the identity and Hopf content from the rigid structure. Its cost is \mathrm{tr}(\mathrm{id}_A) = [2]_q = q + q^{-1} \approx 2.011.
